budget_items.topic: Town Beach fee increase vs. actual revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: The recreation director said the May rate increase brought in more money but not as much as hoped when the in-town rate was raised; the department had expected a larger increase than it is seeing.
The town-appropriated salary line for Town Beach was already mostly spent two and a half weeks into the season; going over it means drawing from the beach revolving account.

budget_items.topic: Day-pass revenue, same date year over year
budget_items.what_was_said: Day-pass money collected by the same date this year was compared to last year to help judge whether an extra open week would be worth the cost.
Total dollar value of beach passes sold so far this year was compared to the full prior year, with the current season not yet finished.
Swim lesson revenue rose year over year even though an afternoon session was dropped, with fewer staff running the program.

budget_items.topic: Cost to staff an extended beach week
budget_items.what_was_said: A bare-minimum two-lifeguard shift for an extra week was estimated in daily salary cost and weighed against whether day-pass sales would cover it.
An unlocked irrigation controller was changed by a user group to run far longer than intended, producing an unusually high water bill; a lockable controller has since been installed.

budget_items.topic: Water district billing detail, Marshall Park
budget_items.what_was_said: Three separate water district charges on the same billing date were reviewed, one much larger than the other two, plus a further large charge the following quarter.
A commissioner noted the school district's community-schools program charges a fee to play in its adult men's basketball league, seen as competing revenue with Parks programming.
The department's outsourced field-mowing contract was described as recently renewed for a multi-year term, itemized by field, with overage billing when extra mowings are required.

decisions.decision: Hold off deciding whether to extend the Town Beach season until more revenue and weather data come in and the town accountant can weigh in.
Not to sign the draft library space-use agreement yet; wait to hear the library trustees' specific concerns first.
Lock all park irrigation controllers and check them periodically following the Marshall Park billing incident.
Ask facilities to identify which field each water bill on the budget report corresponds to.
Target the Town Beach renaming ceremony for around September 10th, pending the sign's completion and family availability.
Move the next scheduled September meeting from the 23rd to the 30th due to member absences.

what_happened.line: Parks Commission tabled extending Town Beach's season, saying the May fee increase brought in less than the department expected.
The beach's town-appropriated salary line was already mostly spent partway into the season, meaning any extension would draw from the beach revolving account instead.
An unlocked irrigation controller at Marshall Park was changed by a user group and ran far longer than intended, producing an unusually high water bill.
The commission declined to sign a draft space-use agreement with the library, opting to wait for the library trustees' specific concerns.
The commission voted to appoint a commissioner to the town's Open Space Committee and approved two sets of minutes.

why_it_matters: A Town Beach season extension depends on money not yet in hand: whether fee revenue and day-pass sales catch up, and whether the town accountant confirms the salary line can absorb it.
The Marshall Park water overrun and a request to match each water bill to its field point toward how field/facility costs get tracked and billed going forward, not a settled dollar figure yet.
Any library or school-district space-sharing arrangement is still under discussion, so no agreement currently binds either side.
